paper.title: Multi-messenger observations of a flaring blazar coincident with high-energy neutrino IceCube-170922A
paper.shortTitle: Multi-messenger observations of a flaring blazar coincident wi
paper.authors: The IceCube, Fermi-LAT, MAGIC et al.

thesis: This observation of a neutrino in spatial coincidence with a gamma-ray emitting blazar during an active phase suggests that blazars may be a source of high-energy neutrinos.

reconstruction.scope: abstract-level graph with retained full text

nodes.title: Research question
nodes.body: What phenomenon is supported by the reported observations?

nodes.title: Choose instrument and selection
nodes.body: Its arrival direction was consistent with the location of a known gamma-ray blazar TXS 0506+056, observed to be in a flaring state.

nodes.title: Acquire and analyze observations
nodes.body: Individual astrophysical sources previously detected in neutrinos are limited to the Sun and the supernova 1987A, whereas the origins of the diffuse flux of high-energy cosmic neutrinos remain unidentified.

nodes.title: Primary reported result
nodes.body: These observations characterize the variability and energetics of the blazar and include the first detection of TXS 0506+056 in very-high-energy gamma-rays.

nodes.title: Published conclusion
nodes.body: This observation of a neutrino in spatial coincidence with a gamma-ray emitting blazar during an active phase suggests that blazars may be a source of high-energy neutrinos.
